subject: Orchard Health renewal — commit restructure & scaling playbook
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Amira Khan <amira.khan@orchard.health>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Orchard Health renewal — usage review & proposed next steps

Hi Amira,

Hope you had a good weekend. As we approach the end of Orchard Health's current term (Dec 31), I've attached a short Q3 usage summary so we can align on renewal sizing. A few highlights from Q3:

- Total token consumption: ~1.9B tokens (15% QoQ increase)
- Peak concurrent requests up 2.6x in October due to triage workflows
- Average response latency (p95): 420ms on standard-gen instances

Given the growth profile, we recommend a commit restructure that splits capacity into a base committed pool + burst credits for seasonal surges. Diego and I sketched a proposal (we can share the spreadsheet if helpful).

Would you be available for a 30-minute alignment call this week to walk through the numbers and a few term options (12 vs 24 month)? If helpful, we can include an ops deep-dive from Evelyn to validate performance SLAs.

Attachment: 2026Q3-Orchard-usage_summary.pdf

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0114
Redwood Inference

From: Amira Khan <amira.khan@orchard.health>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-12T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Orchard Health renewal — usage review & proposed next steps

Thanks Mina — the summary is helpful. A couple of quick questions before we set a call:

1) Can you share modeled unit economics for 12 vs 24 month commits (per-1M-token price at each tier)? Our finance team is sensitive to multi-year lock-ins.
2) For burst credits: how are they priced and billed when used (one-time charge vs amortized)?
3) We have a procurement freeze on new long-term commitments until our PO terms are standard — I attached the form procurement requires.

If you can send a draft commit tier and a sample contract addendum, I can loop Tom (Procurement) and our legal. We have availability Thursday afternoon.

Attachment: Orchard-procurement_form.pdf

—Amira
Head of Platform Engineering
Orchard Health
amira.khan@orchard.health

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Amira Khan <amira.khan@orchard.health>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-13T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Orchard Health renewal — usage review & proposed next steps

Hi Amira — great to e-meet you. Per Mina's note, I attached a proposed_commit_plan that includes two options:

Option A — 12 month:
- Committed tokens: 2.1B/year
- Burst credits: 800M (pay-as-used at 0.85x committed unit rate)
- Effective per-1M-token committed price: $34.50
- Onboarding credit: one month of burst free (up to 200M tokens)

Option B — 24 month (preferred unit economics):
- Committed tokens: 2.0B/year (annualized)
- Burst credits: 1.2B/year
- Effective per-1M-token committed price: $28.75
- Commitment credit: 10% off year-one overage

ROI notes (high level): with the 24-month structure we estimate a 22–28% reduction in per-token spend vs current month-to-month usage given predictable traffic and recommended batching settings (we can model your exact prompt mix on the call).

I've also called out required procurement fields in the attached spreadsheet so your procurement team can map to their PO process. Happy to tailor pricing slices if you can share target budget.

Attachment: Orchard-proposed_commit_plan.xlsx

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
diego.fernandez@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0199

From: Amira Khan <amira.khan@orchard.health>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@orchard.health>
Date: 2026-10-14T10:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Orchard Health renewal — usage review & proposed next steps

Diego — thanks for the options. A couple of clarifications from procurement/legal:

- They prefer an amortized overage model rather than one-time bursts charged at list; would Redwood be open to amortizing burst usage over the quarter at the committed unit rate (with a modest uplift)?
- We cannot sign any 24-month term without a performance backstop clause (credits) if p95 latency goes above 600ms for 2 consecutive weeks.

Also: Tom flagged that PO terms must reference the standard Orchard SLA addendum (see attached). If you can provide a short note on how credits would work in the event of SLA misses, that would help get this to legal faster.

Attachment: Orchard-procurement_form.pdf

—Amira

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Amira Khan <amira.khan@orchard.health>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-15T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Orchard Health renewal — usage review & proposed next steps

Hi Amira + team,

Thanks for the procurement context. Quick responses to the two asks:

1) Amortized burst pricing: we can amortize burst consumption over the quarter at the committed unit rate + a 5% uplift (applied monthly) so billing is smoother for finance. We will include this in the contract language.

2) SLA backstop: we can add a service credit table tied to p95 latency for your production routing (we use your tagged route). Example: p95 > 600ms for 2 consecutive weeks = 10% service credit for that billing month. If the issue persists for a month, automatic canary fallback to a lower-latency model variant is triggered and Redwood will provide a remediation credit up to 20% (per terms).

Operational notes: attached is a Q3 performance snapshot extracted from your prod telemetry (route: /orchard/triage). We see median latency at ~210ms with the October surge pushing p95 toward 420–460ms on standard instances — well within the threshold but we understand the sensitivity during peak windows.

Attachment: Q3-performance-snapshot.csv

Proposed next steps: if those two items are acceptable, Diego and Mina can send an updated addendum and redline-friendly contract. We can also schedule a short ops call to validate monitoring hooks.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Manager, Customer Reliability
evelyn.hart@redwood.ai

From: Amira Khan <amira.khan@orchard.health>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@orchard.health>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-21T15:23:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Orchard Health renewal — usage review & proposed next steps

Thanks everyone — that all sounds reasonable and addresses legal/procurement concerns. Orchard is prepared to move forward with Option B (24-month) provided the amortized burst uplift and the SLA credit language you outlined are included. Our procurement team will issue a PO once we have the updated addendum + contract.

Please send the DocuSign link and the final addendum by end of day Thursday and I’ll prioritize the PO. Looking forward to locking this in — we expect another 25% growth over Q1, so the burst pool is important.

Best,
Amira Khan
Head of Platform Engineering
Orchard Health
